Linert Contact Us Contact Advertise Submit News Statement of Values Terms of Service Public Notices Browse notices Place a notice Lifestyles Antibiotic ointment cures foot odor By Joe Graedon, M.S. and Teresa Graedon, Ph.D. July 21, 2026 3 min read Trending Q. It was suggested that I apply a thin coat of antibacterial ointment on my feet when they get smelly. One application keeps the smell away from my feet for months. A. We have been intrigued to learn that over-the-counter antibiotic ointments such as Polysporin (bacitracin and polymyxin B) can sometimes help against nail fungus. That's because some nail infections are bacterial rather than fungal (Journal of the American Podiatric Medical Association, March 1, 2021). Your report suggests that bacteria may also contribute to some cases of foot odor. People should be aware that neomycin, found in Neosporin, may trigger an allergic reaction (contact dermatitis). Q. Why do doctors prescribe so much gabapentin without warning people that it could be bad for their brains? My husband and I have both been prescribed large amounts by several doctors with instructions to take it three times daily. I'm so glad I looked up potential side effects and found that it can increase the chance of dementia or mild cognitive impairment. This is one drug we won't be taking. A. Gabapentin is the most frequently prescribed pain medicine in the U.S., although the Food and Drug Administration has only approved its use for epilepsy and post-shingles pain (postherpetic neuralgia). Nervous system side effects include drowsiness, dizziness, abnormal thinking and amnesia. A recent systematic review in the journal Drugs & Aging (June 22, 2026) concluded that "Gabapentinoid use was associated with modestly higher estimated odds of ADRD [Alzheimer's disease and related dementia] in pooled observational data." This does not demonstrate a cause-and-effect relationship. However, the authors urge colleagues to exercise caution when prescribing gabapentin for "off-label" use. That would include most pain relief prescriptions. Q. I recently began taking atorvastatin for high LDL cholesterol. I haven't been tested yet to see how it's working, but I have had a weird side effect. My butt got really itchy. My stool was a little softer, but not diarrhea. I have a bidet, so I feel confident that everything stays pretty clean down there. But the itching interfered with my sleep. Hydrocortisone and zinc oxide paste helped a little. Then, I ran out of my pills and couldn't get a refill for several days over a long holiday weekend. After about three days, the itching was gone. I am hesitant to start back on the statin and wonder if a lower dose might have fewer side effects. Are there other formulations of statins that might not have this effect? I am concerned about my high LDL and will ask my doctor about testing for LP(a). A. Itching is not listed as a common side effect of atorvastatin, not to mention itching in that specific body part. Nevertheless, Polish investigators have found an association between statins and itching (Advances in Dermatology and Allergology, Oct. 20, 2024). Moreover, there is a case report on statin-associated itching in the journal Cureus (Sept. 10, 2022). A lower dose might help, but there is not enough research on this topic to tell. You should ask your doctor whether a different approach to lowering your LDL might be appropriate. To prepare for that conversation, you might want to read our "eGuide to Cholesterol Control and Heart Health." This online resource may be found under the Health eGuides tab at www.PeoplesPharmacy.com. In their column, Joe and Teresa Graedon answer letters from readers. Photograph: David Dee Delgado/Reuters New York ‘Abolish ICE’: Mamdani, AOC and other Democrats urge action after New York shooting Immigration officer shot man in car where five-year-old child was sitting, sparking fierce protests Auzzy Byrdsell and José Olivares in New York Fri 9 Oct 2026 16.51 EDT First published on Fri 9 Oct 2026 09.09 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Leading New York Democrats expressed anger and demanded curbs on Immigration and Customs Enforcement ( ICE ) violence after a federal officer shot a man driving a car in which his five-year-old son was sitting, sparking fierce protests . At least seven shots were reportedly fired and the man was hit in the neck late on Thursday afternoon as children were coming home from school in the busy Marble Hill neighborhood of New York City. Marble Hill is considered part of Manhattan, but is physically located in the Bronx. Federal authorities on Friday morning identified Oscar Belgal as the man shot, saying he was undocumented, from the Dominican Republic and had a felony record and gang affiliations. ICE agent shoots man in New York City with five-year-old reportedly in car Read more Belgal was later booked into the Metropolitan Detention Center, Brooklyn, federal lockup, which is newly being used to detain immigrants, according to his attorneys and a US prosecutor who spoke during a hearing on Friday afternoon. He still has a “bullet in his body” and has not been able to communicate with his family, his attorneys said during the hearing. ICE took Belgal on Thursday from a New York hospital into New Jersey. He reportedly spent the night inside the Elizabeth Contract Detention Facility, a privately run ICE facility, before being brought back into New York and being booked into MDC Brooklyn. Meanwhile, Belgal was able to have only one phone call with lawyers on Friday, his attorney Paige Austin with Make the Road New York said. A New York federal judge on early Friday morning ordered ICE to keep Belgal in the area, after his attorneys filed emergency motions requesting his release. The justice department is likely to argue that Belgal’s transfer into New Jersey took place before the judge’s order, making the order requiring ICE to keep him in the area moot. And Belgal’s attorneys have indicated that they will continue challenging his detention. The Justice Department will likely argue that Bergal’s transfer into New Jersey took place before the New York judge’s order, which would make the judge’s order requiring ICE to keep him in the area moot. Bergal’s attorneys will continue to challenge his detention. Marcos Charles, a senior ‌ICE official, said Belgal refused ​to exit his car when approached by ‌federal officers who were trying to arrest him, and then accelerated, ‌struck two ICE vehicles and drove towards other officers. An ICE officer then shot Belgal and Charles said the wound was “superficial”. Footage showed a man in a high-visibility construction vest, possibly with a badge on a lanyard, carrying an assault-style rifle and standing close to Belgal, who is sat on the street, while another officer appears to hold a hand to his neck and shoulder area. New York police officers in uniform shortly afterwards carry the man to an unmarked car and lay him in the back seat, handcuffed behind his back. But Kathy Hochul, New York’s governor, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a New York congresswoman, and Zohran Mamdani , the city’s mayor – all of whom are Democrats – led strong condemnation of ICE’s conduct. Darializa Avila Chevalier, the Democratic New York candidate, rushed to the protests and was knocked over in the chaos as local police and demonstrators clashed. View image in fullscreen Darializa Avila Chevalier at a protest after an ICE officer shot a man in New York, on Thursday. Photograph: Olga Fedorova/EPA The wounded man was conscious and hospitalized, authorities said . A joint statement from Bronx and Manhattan borough presidents Vanessa L Gibson and Brad Hoylman-Sigal, respectively, said their constituents “stand united in outrage” over Belgal’s shooting. “The frustration, pain, anger and trauma stoked by this incident extends far beyond an individual,” the statement said. Mamdani called the incident “unconscionable” and said on Thursday night that ICE, part of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), had “whisked him away” from the New York-Presbyterian Allen hospital in upper Manhattan. A similar incident occurred in Texas last month after a man was shot by an ICE officer in Austin and despite a bullet lodged in his back was taken by the federal authorities from a local hospital to ICE detention about 140 miles away. Ocasio-Cortez and Mamdani demanded ICE be abolished. Both Hochul and Mamdani spoke to Donald Trump and Markwayne Mullin, the homeland security secretary, by phone on Thursday night. Gone in 90 seconds: an ‘invisibilized’ ICE is arresting more people than ever Read more “I have been on ​the phone with President Trump and Secretary Mullin negotiating ‌the release of the man ICE agents ‌shot. Those negotiations were unsuccessful,” Mamdani told a press conference. He demanded from the Trump ‌administration that ICE stop its enforcement actions in New York City. “ICE is rotten to its core,” he said. ICE has been stepping up arrests all year despite withdrawing massed militarized ranks from Minneapolis in January and adopting a more covert approach to enforcement . Both Hochul and Mamdani demanded that ICE cease enforcement operations in New York and the governor said she expressed outrage to the Trump administration on behalf of all New Yorkers. Hochul added that the incident could easily have ended in tragedy. “No child should ever have to experience the terror of gunfire,” she said. The child was being looked after by his family on Friday. 1:58 ICE officer shoots man in New York City – video The streets where the shooting and protests took place were calm on Friday morning but many residents remained shocked and angry. “Here’s an innocent child that was caught in the crossfire,” said Calvin Hayden, a south Bronx native. “That child could have been killed.” Hayden heard about the shooting the night before and said he was immediately disturbed. He came to Marble Hill, the northernmost part of Manhattan, to see the aftermath. “I don’t believe ICE has any reason or right to be in New York City,” he said, adding he thought New York was already equipped on its own to handle immigration disputes without ICE presence. “There’s a lot of individuals who are not committing crimes and they just want to make a better life for themselves,” he said. Some drivers on 225th Street yelled anti-ICE sentiments as they drove past the scene. View image in fullscreen A vehicle with a bullet hole and a shattered window at the scene of the shooting. Photograph: David Dee Delgado/Reuters Mullin said on Friday morning that the ICE officers involved in the shooting did not know there was a child in the vehicle and defended the agency’s actions. But he pointed out that Belgal would have obviously known the child was in his car when he drove it at officers. The exact sequence of events leading up to the shooting have not yet become clear. Mullin said that Hochul had asked the DHS for a pause on enforcement in New York. “No, we are not putting a pause on enforcement,” he said. Mullin criticized New York’s “sanctuary” policies , ​which restrict how much city agencies and police cooperate with immigration authoritie. Belgal, 28, has prior convictions, was serving five years of probation for felony grand larceny and was also arrested on drug charges in 2025, a case that is still pending, according to the New York police department. “What happened today was an outrage,” Mamdani said late on Thursday, adding: “When ICE agents opened fire, a five-year-old child – a five-year-old child! – was in the back seat of that car. Thank God that child is physically unharmed.” Witnesses told local media they heard the child yelling at the officers after the shooting. At least 20 people have been shot by federal immigration agents under the second Trump administration, as well as a rise in deaths in detention. Three deaths, three states, 24 hours: one day in ICE’s quiet but ‘gruesome’ surge Read more “ICE is a rogue, lawless and paramilitary surveillance agency. It does not belong in New York City and it should not exist in the United States of America. Abolish ICE,” Ocasio-Cortez said in a statement. The representative also condemned the retail company Target for allowing federal enforcement teams to use its parking lots as staging areas from which to launch arrest operations. Protesters held signs saying:“Jail all killer ICE agents” and “Leave our neighbors alone.” View image in fullscreen Demonstrators protest near the scene of the shooting. Photograph: David Dee Delgado/Reuters “ICE, get the fuck out of our neighborhood,” shouted Gibson, the Bronx borough president. “I’m angry that we have to be here … We are a working-class community. We don’t deserve this type of treatment from the White House.” She encouraged the crowd to get involved in opposing ICE, saying: “There are more of us than there are of them. I want this to be a moment that we turn into a movement.” Protesters gathered at the hospital where Belgal was taken. The police set up barricades and protesters quickly clashed with officers in a chaotic scene. Demonstrators banged drums and shouted: “Shut it down,” and “ICE out!” as cars driving by honked in support. Standing outside the hospital, Murad Awawdeh, the president of the New York Immigration Coalition, said he wanted to see an independent investigation into the shooting led by New York officials. “The pain that you’re witnessing is people who are witnessing their neighbors, their family members, their friends being ripped away,” he said. ICE has arrested more than 19,500 people in New York and nearly 18,000 in New Jersey during the second Trump administration, mostly Latin American immigrant men without criminal histories, Gothamist reported earlier this week using government data, adding that those totals were more than double the number of such arrests in the last 18 months of the Biden administration. Photograph: Yong Teck Lim/Getty Images Technology ‘Black October’: cybersecurity experts sound the alarm over new era of AI-enabled hacking After discovery of severe bug in the PHP programming language, executives warn of ‘vulnerability tsunami’ Johana Bhuiyan Fri 23 Oct 2026 14.48 EDT Last modified on Fri 23 Oct 2026 14.59 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Leaders in cybersecurity are sounding the alarm after the discovery of a major vulnerability this week. They are predicting that artificial intelligence tools will expose more fundamental weaknesses in global internet infrastructure in the months to come. “I no longer think we’re going to be able to patch all bugs,” said Sam Altman on Thursday evening, joining the chorus of executives. In the midst of what’s being called “Black October”, for which researchers used AI to help identify critical flaws in a coding language that is used across millions of websites and may have been unpatched for years, tech executives are warning about the ways AI will be used both to identify and exploit security vulnerabilities at an unprecedented scale and pace. The next few months will see a “vulnerability tsunami”, according to Jason Clinton, Anthropic’s deputy chief information security officer. “There won’t be enough time to patch critical infrastructure,” Clinton said in a post on X on Thursday evening. Marc Benioff, the Salesforce CEO, agreed and called it a “code red”. AI is uniquely able to find and identify security flaws in a way and at a pace that will feel catastrophic because the security community will not be able to move quickly enough to address them, said Matthew Prince, the Cloudflare CEO. “It’s going to feel like the sky is falling. It’s going to feel like there’s nothing we can do. “The next two years are going to be incredibly, incredibly, incredibly fraught with new tools that have infinite patience to go look for vulnerabilities across the Internet,” he wrote in a post on X. While cybersecurity experts have been warning about a “vulnpocalypse”, or the ability for AI to more easily identify security bugs for months, it wasn’t until “Black October” that researchers were able to use AI to find a flaw as fundamental and critical as the one announced on 21 October. Massive bugs were found in a programming language called PHP, which may have left the millions of websites that run on it vulnerable to hackers for years. Some experts estimated 70% of all the sites on the internet were at risk of hacking. However, in the same way AI will be used to aid in identifying security vulnerabilities at an unprecedented pace, tech leaders worry it’ll also be used by malicious actors to exploit those bugs at an unprecedented pace. Attempts to exploit the PHP vulnerability have already begun . After the vulnerabilities were announced, government and private websites across the US and UK temporarily took down their sites to patch the bugs. The US National Security Agency (NSA) issued an alert recommending any site that runs on PHP implement the patches immediately. Malicious cyberactors may seek to further exploit these bugs to access servers without authorization, the NSA said. “Such an access vector could help attackers steal sensitive data, disrupt services or move deeper into a network,” the warning read. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to TechScape A weekly dive in to how technology is shaping our lives after newsletter promotion In a post on X, Prince said CloudFlare, a security provider, had seen evidence of thousands of people trying to exploit the PHP flaws in the 10 hours before it was announced. “That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours, and millions now,” he wrote. In a blogpost, researchers at AI security platform Wiz said that this was “among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history”. “The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve,” they wrote.
